mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month indicates an easing monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by more than 0.2% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings growth and causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in 60% or more of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a weakening economy with falling output and rising joblessness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in 60% or more of instances where INDPRO falls and UNRATE rises.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals reduced consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp and RSAFS falls.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening consumer demand and economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where HOUST increases by more than 1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL reading above 2.5% annualized signals elevated inflation, prompting potential Federal Reserve tightening and negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in 60% or more of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a robust labor market, boosting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong economic expansion (GDPC1 growth > 3% annualized), a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in 60% or more of instances where GDPC1 growth exceeds 3% and RSAFS declines.
